main.title: Crash: Mind over Mutant
main.subtitle: Keep a mutant in reserve and bring its powers back to the island
main.summary: Crash: Mind over Mutant is Radical Entertainment's 2008 follow-up to Crash of the Titans. Cortex and N. Brio use a fashionable electronic device to control the minds of bandicoots and mutants. Crash explores Wumpa Island with Aku Aku, freeing creatures and borrowing their powers. Activision announced its shipment to North American retailers on 7 October 2008.

cards.heading: Cortex puts a device in every hand
cards.text: Crash: Mind over Mutant is Radical Entertainment's 2008 follow-up to Crash of the Titans. Cortex and N. Brio use a fashionable electronic device to control the minds of bandicoots and mutants. Crash explores Wumpa Island with Aku Aku, freeing creatures and borrowing their powers. Activision announced its shipment to North American retailers on 7 October 2008.

cards.heading: A power kept for later
cards.text: The central change is the ability to store a captured mutant and summon it later. A creature can therefore become part of a plan that extends beyond the fight where it was found. Crash can switch between his own movements and a saved companion's abilities, while collected Mojo develops their strength. Grimly slows time, for example, and RhinoRoller curls into a rolling form. Their powers make a familiar route behave differently.

cards.heading: Returning with a different companion
cards.text: The island connects areas that Crash visits again as his objectives develop. Conversations, a mission list and a map provide directions through this returning journey. New companions can help with obstacles that were encountered earlier, giving the choice of mutant a role in exploration. Retracing these paths also affects the pacing: a useful power and a new destination can still require travelling through ground the player already knows. The adventure asks the player to remember routes as well as attacks.

cards.heading: Comedy and company
cards.text: The story uses animated scenes with deliberately different cartoon treatments, extending its jokes beyond the characters' spoken exchanges. On the home-console versions, another player can join as Coco and help explore or fight alongside Crash. The shared view makes keeping together part of the arrangement. Radical's game appeared on PlayStation 2, Wii and Xbox 360.

main.title: Dead Space
main.subtitle: Fear Is Written on Your Back
main.summary: Engineer Isaac Clarke enters the USG Ishimura with tools that become weapons and a suit that carries the information needed to survive.

cards.heading: A repair mission aboard the Ishimura
cards.text: Dead Space arrived on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in North America on October 14, 2008, with PC following on October 20. EA Redwood Shores sends engineer Isaac Clarke aboard the mining ship USG Ishimura, where a repair mission becomes a struggle against Necromorphs. Industrial tools serve as weapons, and health and equipment information appear on Isaac's suit or as projections in the world.

cards.heading: An engineer's tools
cards.text: Isaac's work equipment shapes how he survives. The Plasma Cutter becomes a weapon while retaining the appearance and cutting function of an industrial tool. His protective suit also belongs to that working environment. Repairing and moving through the ship depend on the same skills and equipment that he turns against its creatures.

cards.heading: Cutting the Necromorphs' limbs
cards.text: Fighting Necromorphs means aiming for limbs to limit their movement and attacks. The shape of an approaching creature determines where a cut will help, and some remain dangerous after losing part of their body. Ammunition and distance matter as Isaac chooses the orientation of the Plasma Cutter and tries to stop an attack before it reaches him.

cards.heading: Reading Isaac's suit
cards.text: The suit displays health along Isaac's back. Menus and other indicators appear as projections beside him, keeping information in the same view as the ship. Interface designer Dino Ignacio described this as a solution developed alongside the rest of the game. Reading equipment or checking health remains connected to Isaac's position in the room.

cards.heading: The ship's working spaces
cards.text: Medical, industrial and residential sectors suggest the work and daily life that once filled the Ishimura. Its corridors connect spaces with recognisable functions as well as encounters with enemies. Equipment and traces of the disaster reveal the ship's history while the layout controls the pace of exploration.

cards.heading: Slowing threats with Stasis
cards.text: Stasis temporarily slows creatures and moving machinery. It can create time to aim at a fast enemy or pass a dangerous mechanism, but its limited energy requires planning. The ability serves both combat and obstacle-solving, extending the practical role of Isaac's engineering tools.

cards.heading: Listening to the Ishimura
cards.text: Ventilation, machinery and impacts give the Ishimura a continuous soundscape. A distant noise may belong to the ship or signal an approaching creature, making the player listen even during an empty corridor. Changes in ambience build tension ahead of a visible threat.

main.title: Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia
main.subtitle: A new order against Dracula
main.summary: Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia is Konami's Nintendo DS action role-playing game starring Shanoa, a member of an organisation seeking a defence against Dracula. After a disrupted ritual costs her memories and emotions, she pursues stolen magical glyphs. The adventure travels through forests, mountains, sea routes and other locations linked by a world map. This structure gives the journey a different shape from one continuous castle. Each destination presents another part of the search while Shanoa gradually acquires the abilities needed to push farther through it.

cards.heading: A new order against Dracula
cards.text: Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia is Konami's Nintendo DS action role-playing game starring Shanoa, a member of an organisation seeking a defence against Dracula. After a disrupted ritual costs her memories and emotions, she pursues stolen magical glyphs. The adventure travels through forests, mountains, sea routes and other locations linked by a world map. This structure gives the journey a different shape from one continuous castle. Each destination presents another part of the search while Shanoa gradually acquires the abilities needed to push farther through it.

cards.heading: Weapons written on the body
cards.text: Shanoa collects glyphs that can be equipped to her arms and back, supplying weapons, spells and other powers. Their use consumes magic points, which refill when she stops attacking. A combination therefore has to suit both the enemy and the rhythm of available energy. Glyph Union techniques combine equipped symbols into a stronger attack that spends hearts instead. The system links a large collection of abilities to a small number of active choices, making preparation and the timing of an opening equally important during a difficult fight.

cards.heading: Beyond the next combat encounter
cards.text: Some glyphs also solve environmental problems, extending the same collection into exploration. Side quests supply additional reasons to revisit locations and earn rewards, while completing the adventure opens challenges such as a boss rush and another playable character. The world map lets the player understand the search as a series of distinct places. Order of Ecclesia gives Shanoa a particularly coherent identity through its mechanics: the symbols she recovers are both the tools with which she fights and the means of uncovering more of the world.

main.title: The Legend of Spyro: Dawn of the Dragon
main.summary: Spyro and Cynder share a magical tether, a larger world and a two-player journey built around combining their different elemental powers.

cards.heading: The game
cards.text: The Legend of Spyro: Dawn of the Dragon is Etranges Libellules' 2008 action adventure for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, PlayStation 2 and Wii. It concludes the Legend trilogy with Spyro and Cynder bound together by a magical tether. Cooperative play and flight broaden their movement as they face Malefor and the approaching destruction of their world.

cards.heading: Two dragons on one tether
cards.text: A second player can take control of the other dragon, while a solo player switches between the pair. The tether keeps them connected, so moving through a space means considering the partner's position. One dragon can reach towards a ledge while the other follows, and a fight can be approached from two nearby directions. The bond is both a story device and a visible constraint, keeping the partnership present when the player is thinking about the next route or enemy.

cards.heading: Take the route into the air
cards.text: The dragons can take flight through permitted areas, lifting exploration away from the ground routes of the earlier games. A broad valley offers room to look for another landing place or approach an objective from above. Enclosed passages and scripted encounters still shape where the pair can travel, so height becomes another part of reading the route. The change gives the journey a wider sense of space while keeping Spyro and Cynder moving through it together.

cards.heading: Choose whose power to use
cards.text: Spyro's fire, ice, electricity and earth sit alongside Cynder's poison, fear, wind and shadow. Switching dragon changes the available response to an enemy or obstacle, and equipment found along the journey can add further bonuses. The two health displays keep the partner's condition visible during a fight. Cooperation can mean drawing attention, finding another angle or choosing the power that best opens the encounter, making the distinction between the dragons useful beyond their different colours and silhouettes.

main.title: Fable II
main.summary: Fable II is a 2008 action role-playing video game developed by Lionhead Studios and published by Microsoft Game Studios for Xbox 360.

cards.text: Fable II is a 2008 action role-playing video game developed by Lionhead Studios and published by Microsoft Game Studios for Xbox 360. The game is the second installment in the Fable game series, and the sequel to 2004's Fable. The story takes place within the fictional land of Albion, 500 years after the first game. Players assume the role of a young hero who is destined to stop a former ruler turned madman from destroying the world. The game features several prominent actors portraying major characters in the game, including Zoë Wanamaker, Ron Glass and Stephen Fry. The game's setting takes inspiration from the historical late colonial era, in terms of architecture, social equality and basic firearms such as flintlock pistols.

The game made several improvements over its predecessor, updating existing gameplay and offering larger locations to explore. Alongside the main story, players can engage in several side quests and repeatable jobs to earn money and rewards, build up a property empire, and customise their character with various clothing items, hairstyles, tattoos and makeup. Players also can make decisions on how they act, affecting their characters' morality and appearance as a result. New features to the game included the opportunity to choose between playing as a male or female character, a fast-travel system, and a canine companion who can detect treasures and alert the player to nearby enemies.

Fable II received critical acclaim after its October 2008 release. Reviewers welcomed its larger world and changes to the original systems. Two downloadable expansions added locations, items and quests and were included in the 2009 Game of the Year edition. Fable III followed in 2010.

main.title: Guitar Hero World Tour
main.subtitle: Guitar Hero makes room for the whole band
main.summary: World Tour added drums, vocals and a music studio to the series’ guitar-and-bass performance.

cards.heading: Beyond the guitar solo
cards.text: Guitar Hero World Tour arrived in North America on October 26, 2008, bringing drums and vocals into the main Guitar Hero series alongside lead guitar and bass. Neversoft led development, with other studios responsible for particular versions. Its 86-song disc selection uses master recordings, and four players can build a band around different musical roles. The new drum controller adds raised cymbal pads, while a revised guitar introduces a touch-sensitive section for particular passages.

cards.heading: A studio inside the game
cards.text: Music Studio lets players use the instrument controllers to construct instrumental songs. The accompanying GHTunes service originally allowed those creations to be shared. Character, instrument and band customisation extend the options for assembling a performance of their own.

main.title: LittleBigPlanet
main.summary: LittleBigPlanet is a 2008 platform video game developed by Media Molecule and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3.

cards.text: LittleBigPlanet is a 2008 platform video game developed by Media Molecule and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3. In LittleBigPlanet, the player controls Sackboy, a customizable ragged doll as they explore the titular realm. The game is primarily centered around content creation, with examples including a level editor and the Popit, a portable menu used for accessing creation tools. Prior to 12 March 2021, the player could publish levels online and play others' published levels. The story mode consists of eight themed areas, in which Sackboy helps out various Creator Curators across LittleBigPlanet before fighting the Collector, who has been kidnapping and stealing creations.

Media Molecule was formed by four former Lionhead Studios employees after the release of Rag Doll Kung Fu in 2005. Wanting to create a video game centered around content creation, they pitched a prototype called Craftworld  to Sony Computer Entertainment Worldwide Studios president Phil Harrison, who lauded the concept and agreed to fund the project. LittleBigPlanet was first announced by Harrison at Game Developers Conference 2007, followed by a marketing campaign, beta testing, and consumer and press anticipation. After brief delay to remove controversial lyrics from an in-game licensed song, LittleBigPlanet released worldwide between October and November 2008.

LittleBigPlanet was met with critical acclaim, with praise for its creative gameplay and community-driven aspects. LittleBigPlanet won several Game of the Year awards and additional awards for its graphics, music, and gameplay innovation. Retrospectively, some publications have ranked it among the greatest video games of all time. After dwindling sales in 2008, LittleBigPlanet became commercially successful, reaching 4.5 million copies.  LittleBigPlanet was followed by two sequels and several spin-offs.

main.title: MotorStorm: Pacific Rift
main.subtitle: The festival reaches an island
main.summary: MotorStorm: Pacific Rift is Evolution Studios' PlayStation 3 off-road racer, first released in North America on 28 October 2008. The second MotorStorm leaves the original game's desert for an island of forests, water, rock and volcanic terrain. Motorcycles, buggies, trucks and other vehicle classes race together on routes with different surfaces and openings. Their differences give a crowded event its shape: a line that suits a light vehicle may expose it to a much heavier opponent. The island changes both the scenery and the decisions made during a lap.

cards.heading: The festival reaches an island
cards.text: MotorStorm: Pacific Rift is Evolution Studios' PlayStation 3 off-road racer, first released in North America on 28 October 2008. The second MotorStorm leaves the original game's desert for an island of forests, water, rock and volcanic terrain. Motorcycles, buggies, trucks and other vehicle classes race together on routes with different surfaces and openings. Their differences give a crowded event its shape: a line that suits a light vehicle may expose it to a much heavier opponent. The island changes both the scenery and the decisions made during a lap.

cards.heading: Read the ground before boosting
cards.text: The player uses boost to gain speed while watching the engine's rising temperature. Keeping it active too long risks destroying the vehicle, so its use becomes a sequence of short judgements rather than a permanent accelerator. Water and hot environments affect that balance, making the surface part of the race's timing. Branching routes allow a smaller machine to take a narrow line while larger vehicles force a way through rougher ground. Choosing where to go matters alongside choosing when to commit to another burst of speed.

cards.heading: More vehicles in the same room
cards.text: Monster trucks join the vehicle selection, able to climb over smaller competitors and break through parts of the environment. Riders on motorcycles and quad bikes face a different version of that physical contest, with less protection when opponents close in. Four-player split-screen brings the mixed field into local multiplayer, while additional event types vary the festival's objectives. The game also allowed music stored on the PlayStation 3 to accompany a race. Its expanded terrain and local racing options developed the festival idea before Apocalypse moved it into a collapsing city.

main.title: Fallout 3
main.subtitle: The First Light Outside the Vault
main.summary: Bethesda opens the Capital Wasteland to first- and third-person exploration, with V.A.T.S. keeping probabilities and character statistics within combat.

cards.heading: Leaving Vault 101
cards.text: Fallout 3 launched in North America on October 28, 2008 for PC, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. Bethesda Game Studios brought the role-playing series into first- and third-person exploration. After leaving Vault 101, the player crosses the ruins of Washington and the Capital Wasteland, meeting settlements and factions while searching for their missing father.

cards.heading: Growing up underground
cards.text: The opening follows the protagonist through childhood and adolescence inside Vault 101. Attribute choices, conversations and the G.O.A.T. test introduce character creation through events within this closed community. When the father disappears and the Vault falls into crisis, leaving it opens a much larger territory after those first hours underground.

cards.heading: Choosing shots with V.A.T.S.
cards.text: The player can aim directly or activate V.A.T.S. to select targets and body parts. Hit probabilities and Action Point costs determine which sequence of shots can be attempted. The system brings the character's statistics into visible decisions during combat, linking the new viewpoint to the series' role-playing rules.

cards.heading: The ruins of Washington
cards.text: Washington's monuments and government buildings remain recognisable among the ruins. Their silhouettes help with orientation, while damaged streets and tunnels complicate the route to them. Exploring the city means discovering how its surviving landmarks and infrastructure have changed since the war.

cards.heading: Decisions across the Wasteland
cards.text: Settlements, mercenaries, the Brotherhood of Steel and the Enclave present competing interests. Decisions in quests and conversations can change access to people, rewards and places. Karma records some of these actions, while the freedom to approach locations in different orders affects when the player encounters a dilemma.

cards.heading: The Pip-Boy and the radio
cards.text: The Pip-Boy 3000 holds the inventory, statistics, map, radio and quest records in a wrist-mounted computer. Its green display fits the world's retrofuturist equipment. Radio music and Galaxy News Radio broadcasts can accompany travel, giving exploration a continuing connection to voices beyond the immediate surroundings.

cards.heading: Rebuilding Fallout for a new viewpoint
cards.text: Bethesda rebuilt the series' systems for its new viewpoint, including V.A.T.S., dialogue and lockpicking. The continuous world shares an approach with The Elder Scrolls, while SPECIAL attributes, retrofuturist humour and consequential decisions maintain ties to earlier Fallout games. The result established the foundation for expansions and later entries.

main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2008
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2008 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.
